subject.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution

question: Should this PR replace wake-time bootstrap for explicit external-plugin heartbeat targets with startup/reload/requested-override preactivation?
rationale: The code now addresses the prior correctness findings, but the remaining tradeoff is a compatibility-sensitive runtime boundary: existing external-plugin heartbeat delivery stops rediscovering plugins on each tick and relies on lifecycle preactivation instead.

options.title: Accept lifecycle preactivation
options.body: Merge after exact-head CI is green if maintainers accept startup, reload, and requested-override preactivation as the supported explicit external-plugin heartbeat boundary.

options.title: Require more live plugin proof
options.body: Ask for one more run where an explicit external plugin target starts outside the active registry and is delivered after preactivation without wake-time bootstrap.

options.title: Keep wake-time bootstrap
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers decide the previous retry/discovery behavior remains the compatibility contract despite the latency risk.

recommendation.title: Accept lifecycle preactivation
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head CI is green if maintainers accept startup, reload, and requested-override preactivation as the supported explicit external-plugin heartbeat boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and verified the predecessor bootstrap behavior that defines the compatibility boundary this PR changes.
